quests.title: Fourth Peg
quests.description: The camp is named for the stake it is pitched around. Learn why there are four.
quests.accept_text:
You came down the north gate, so you have walked about nine miles of this and you will have noticed there is no road.

There was one. It is in a hole. I am not here to build you a new one - I am here to find out whether a new one is POSSIBLE, which is a different job with a different answer, and only one of those has ever been funded.

Stand by the peg a moment. Everything this camp does is measured from that stake.
quests.turn_in_text:
Seven months, that one has stood. The longest any of them has managed.

If you are going to be out in it, I can use you. Everything we need is a reading taken somewhere I would rather not send Hask on his own.

quests.title: The Level Run
quests.description: Run the level west from the peg and come back with the ground under it.
quests.accept_text:
A level run is two people and a long walk and it is the dullest work in the world right up until it is not.

I need the ground between here and Cartfall, in a straight line, which means walking it rather than going round. Mind the shrikes - they nest where the ground is thin and they have opinions about company.
quests.turn_in_text:
Good numbers. Boring numbers, which out here is the only kind worth having - and three years ago there were no numbers at all, because nobody had thought to take any.

What I cannot write down is the other thing. The hardpan RINGS different over a void. Not much. It is louder in the cold. I have been trying to put that in a book for two years and it keeps coming out sounding like a man guessing.

quests.title: What Hask Hears
quests.description: Test the thing he cannot write down, in the one place it can be checked.
quests.accept_text:
There is one way to test me and you are going to hate it: the crawlers come up through the thin ground. Where they are thickest is where the roof is worst.

So. Go where I say the hardpan rings wrong, count what comes out at you, and bring me the plates. If I am right you will have a bad afternoon and I will have a method.
quests.turn_in_text:
Five. You got five off a stretch I called thin, and Peska's rod came back at eleven on the stretch either side of it.

That is not proof. It is the first thing I have had that is even the same SHAPE as proof.

quests.title: Come Back in Four Days
quests.description: A survey is one reading taken twice, and the second reading is the whole job.
quests.accept_text:
Anybody can take a reading. A reading is a number and a number on its own cannot tell you whether ground is going anywhere.

Two readings, four days apart, at the same stake: THAT tells you. We have been doing it for two years and I have nine hundred pairs of numbers and about four of them matter.

Take the second pass on the Wide Sink and Nineteen Mile. And bring me ooze residue - they eat limestone, and I want to know how fast.
quests.turn_in_text:
The Wide Sink has moved eleven inches in four days. Eleven inches is nothing to look at and it is enormous in a column.

That rim is still going. Four years on, and the hole we all think of as finished is not finished.

quests.title: The Second Peg
quests.description: The top of a survey stake, snapped off, with a number still on it.

objectives.label: the snapped peg head, to Chief Surveyor Vane

quests.accept_text: It is the top four inches of a proper survey stake, driven and then broken off about a foot above where it was driven. There is a number burned into it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Two. That is Second Peg, and Second Peg is sitting on the lip of the Wide Sink being perfectly accurate about a place that is not there any more.

Somebody broke the head off it. That was not the ground. Somebody stood out there and snapped the top off a survey stake, and I have no idea who or why and I think about it more than I should.

quests.title: Whether, Not How
quests.description: Enough readings to say something careful, finally.
quests.accept_text: I have two years of pairs and I am close to being able to say a sentence I can defend. I would like one more set from the south, where the revenants are, and then I am going to say it whether the port likes it or not.
quests.turn_in_text:
Here it is, and you may tell Rullo Tack I said it.

A road is possible. A road is NOT possible on a twenty-year bond, which is the only kind anybody will finance, because this field is still opening and four of my eleven are still moving.

So the honest answer is: ask me again in ten years. Nobody has ever paid a surveyor to say that and I expect it will cost me the contract.

quests.title: He Was On the Box
quests.description: The teamster who came off the back of a cart that kept going down.
quests.accept_text:
Nineteen Mile. I was on the box and the lead pair were six lengths ahead of me when it went.

I did not do anything clever. The cart went down and I came off the back of it and the ground I landed on held. That is the whole story and I have told it four hundred times.

What I would like is for the scavengers to stop going through it. They are at the rim of that hole every day and there are people in it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thank you. I know what they are. They came through with everything else and found a desert full of carts with nobody guarding them, and I would probably be doing the same.

I would still rather they did it somewhere else.

quests.title: The Lead Pair
quests.description: The beasts went in ahead of the cart and some of them came back out.
quests.accept_text:
The kodo that went down are not all dead. Some of them came out the other side of something down there and they are not right, and they are the ones you see on the flats with harness still on them.

Cut the harness off what you have to put down. Bring it to me. It is a house mark and somebody should know whose.
quests.turn_in_text:
[He goes through the straps one at a time without hurrying.]

This one is Tarrow's. This one is Tarrow's. This one I do not know.

I will write to Steamwheedle. It is four years late and I am going to do it anyway.

quests.title: Still Walking the Line
quests.description: The drovers are still on the route, in the sense that nobody ever called them off.
quests.accept_text:
I cooked for caravans for eleven years before this and I will tell you the thing about drovers: they do not stop. Weather, raiders, a broken axle - the road keeps going and so do they.

The ones out there still have not stopped. Bring me their tags. I want to cook for a camp that has done right by them, and we have not.
quests.turn_in_text:
I knew two of these. Not well. Well enough to know how they take their tea, which is the sort of thing you know about a drover.

Peska will put the numbers in the book. I am going to do something else about it, and I am not going to tell you what because it is not your business and it is not hers either.

quests.title: The Cart That Never Arrived
quests.description: A sealed manifest for freight that is somewhere under the First Hole.

objectives.label: the sealed waybill, to Quartermaster Lund

quests.accept_text: A cargo manifest, still sealed, for a cart that is not going to arrive. The wax is intact, which after four years in a desert is its own small miracle.
quests.turn_in_text:
[He breaks the seal, reads it, and sets it down.]

Seed grain. Forty bushels of seed grain for Gadgetzan, dated the spring the wells went.

Somebody in that city ordered seed. In the second dry season, with the well dropping, somebody sat down and ordered next year's seed.

I am going to keep this. I do not entirely know why.

quests.title: What the Birds Know
quests.description: A shrike's crop is a survey of what is living where nobody can look.
quests.accept_text:
Here is a free method and it is not mine, it is every rodman's: open the bird.

A shrike hunts the thin ground and the rim and it will eat anything it can carry. What is in its crop is a list of what is living in a place you cannot get to.

Six crops will tell me more about the floor of those holes than Vizzi's rope has in a year, and I would like that on record before I say it to her face.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four of six had something in them from below the water line. From a WATER line, in the Abyssal Sands, where there has not been standing water in living memory.

She is going to be insufferable. She has been saying there is water down there for a year.

quests.title: Twenty-Two Tiles in an Afternoon
quests.description: The newest hole on the map, and the longest.

objectives.label: the north rim of the Long Collapse

quests.accept_text:
The Long Collapse opened eleven months ago, over about four hours, and it took twenty-two tiles of ground and a stretch of the old road with it.

It is the only one any of us watched happen. I want the rim walked and I want it walked by somebody who is not me, because I have walked it nine times and I have stopped seeing it.
quests.turn_in_text:
You can walk the length of that one and never be more than a step from the edge, and three years ago it was road.

That is in my book now, in those words, which is not how I usually write. Some things want saying plainly.

quests.title: Nine of the Eleven
quests.description: Somebody has to go down them, and she has been doing it alone.
quests.accept_text:
Somebody has to go down them. Not far - far enough to see whether there is a floor and whether the floor is going anywhere.

Nine of the eleven have floors. Two do not. I would like a second pair of hands on the line and I would like them attached to somebody who can fight, because the floors are not empty.
quests.turn_in_text:
Peska logs the two as 'no bottom observed'. I would log them differently. I would log them as 'do not'.

None of the eleven existed three years ago. People forget that, out here, as fast as they can.

She is being careful and I am being accurate and we have agreed to disagree about which of those is the job.

quests.title: Up Through the Floor
quests.description: The holes did not only swallow.
quests.accept_text:
Everybody out here talks about what went IN. Four years of it. The carts, the kodo, the road.

Nobody wants to talk about what came OUT, and I have been down nine of these on a rope, and I am telling you that the crawlers and the oozes were not living on this desert four years ago because this desert could not feed them.

The holes opened a way. It goes both directions.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thin them where they come up and you buy the camp a week. You do not buy it two.

Before the change there was nothing under this desert that wanted to be above it.

I have stopped pretending this is a problem that gets solved. It is a problem that gets managed by people who are still here, and that is me.

quests.title: Four Days From the Nearest Brine
quests.description: The revenants are salt-cured and there is no salt out here.
quests.accept_text:
I am a brewer, so I know what brine does to a bone, and the things coming up out of the southern holes are BRINE-CURED.

The nearest brine is the Shimmering Flats and that is four days' walk northwest. Either somebody is carrying salt out here for a purpose I do not want to think about, or there is brine under us.
quests.turn_in_text:
Under us. It has to be under us, and it has been coming this way for three years.

The pan is four days northwest and everybody there will tell you the water goes under and goes EAST. We are east. We have always been east. Nobody ever stopped to ask what it was going through on the way.

quests.title: No Bottom Observed
quests.description: The two holes with no floor, and what comes up them.
quests.accept_text:
The Throats are the two with no floor and they are the two I will not go down past forty feet.

There is something living in them that is WET. I need scale off whatever you can reach, and somebody else has to be holding the knife, because I been down that hole nine times and the tenth is where people stop coming back.
quests.turn_in_text:
Still wet. It has been in a bag, in a desert, for a day, and it is still wet.

There is water down there. Not damp - water, enough of it to keep something that size alive. Everybody in this camp has been walking over it for two years.

quests.title: What Is Feeding Them
quests.description: Nothing in this zone is native to a desert, which is the point.
quests.accept_text:
Go through the bestiary of this place with me. Crawlers: cave animal. Oozes: cave animal. The horrors in the Throats: aquatic. The revenants: brine.

There is not one thing on this map that belongs in a desert except the shrikes, and the shrikes are here because everything ELSE is here.

The entire population of this zone is a consequence of the water leaving. Bring me enough residue to say that with a number on it.
quests.turn_in_text:
A number. Finally a number.

That is not a desert bestiary with some cave animals in it. That is a cave bestiary that has had its roof taken off.

quests.title: Managed, Not Solved
quests.description: Buy the camp another week, properly this time.
quests.accept_text:
Peska wants the readings. Hask wants his method. Odd wants the scavengers off the rim.

I want the camp to still be here in a month, and that is a different list and it is mostly killing.

I am not going to dress it up. Go and make the ground round this peg quiet for a while.
quests.turn_in_text:
Quiet. For a while.

That is the whole job and anybody who tells you different has not been here two years.

quests.title: One Face of It Is Glass
quests.description: The south face of one pit is fused, and nothing out here is hot enough.
quests.accept_text:
The Glasswall. South face, about sixty feet of it, fused solid - proper glass, you can see yourself in it in the afternoon.

Sand goes to glass at about three thousand degrees. There is nothing in this desert that gets to three thousand degrees, there is no volcanic rock within a hundred miles, and lightning does not do sixty feet in a line.

Go and look at it and tell me what you think, because I have run out of things to think.
quests.turn_in_text: It is not weathered. That is the part. Three years of sand on glass and the face is still smooth, which means it happened AFTER the hole opened, not before.

quests.title: Still Warm
quests.description: Shards off the fused face, still warm hours after sundown.
quests.accept_text:
I have had a shard of that face on my bench for a month and it is WARM. Not hot. Warm, at midnight, in a desert that goes to freezing.

Bring me five more and I will find out whether it is the stone or whether it is something in the stone, and I would like it to be the stone.
quests.turn_in_text:
It is not the stone.

I have crushed one, dissolved one, and left one in the dark for a week, and the one in the dark is the warmest of the three. Whatever is in that glass is not being heated. It is heating.

quests.title: It Throws the Afternoon Back
quests.description: You can see the Glasswall from the camp at the right hour, and the camp has opinions.
quests.accept_text:
Twice a year the sun gets the angle right and that face throws the whole afternoon back at us, and for about forty minutes this camp is the brightest place in Tanaris.

Tobbit says it is a hazard. Hask says it is beautiful. I say it is the only thing out here that does anything on a schedule and I will not have it spoken of badly.
quests.turn_in_text: There. Now I can stand and watch it without something coming up the rise at me, which is all I have ever wanted out of that wall.

quests.title: Nothing Out Here Is Hot Enough
quests.description: Put the Glasswall in the book properly, with the thing nobody wants to write.
quests.accept_text:
I have to write up that face and I have been putting it off for seven months, because the honest entry is 'cause unknown' and I have never written that in a book with my name on it.

Get me enough of it that 'cause unknown' comes with six samples and a date, which is the difference between an admission and a finding.
quests.turn_in_text:
'Cause unknown. Sixty feet, south-facing, post-collapse, six samples, no local heat source identified.'

There. It is in. I feel worse than I expected and better than I deserve.

quests.title: The Wrong Direction for a Hole
quests.description: The easternmost pit has light coming up out of it.
quests.accept_text:
East pit. Underlight, which is what the camp calls it and what Peska has grudgingly started calling it in the book.

There is light coming UP out of that hole. Not much - you cannot see it at noon - but stand on the rim after dark and you can read by it, and light does not come up out of the ground.

Go and stand on it. Everybody has to once.
quests.turn_in_text:
Everybody who looks in wants to go in. That is the part nobody says out loud and it is true of every single person in this camp including me.

That light was not there before the change. Nothing here was.

quests.title: Lit From Below
quests.description: Work out what is making the light, which means getting close to it.
quests.accept_text:
It is not fire. Fire flickers and that does not. It is not the glass - wrong colour and wrong place.

What it IS doing is getting slightly brighter every season, which I have measured, and I would like a sample of everything living within forty feet of it before I say anything about that in front of Peska.
quests.turn_in_text:
Every single thing within forty feet of that pit is wet, and the further east you go the wetter they get.

East. Everything about this zone points east and the camp is pitched in the northeast corner and I do not think that was an accident on Peska's part, whatever she says.

quests.title: The Two Without Floors
quests.description: Both bottomless pits are on the east side, and east is where the ground is worst.
quests.accept_text:
Nine have floors. Two do not. Both of the two are east.

I have been down both to the end of my line and the line is a hundred and twenty feet and it does not reach anything.

Walk both rims for me in one day, in order, and tell me whether you come back thinking what I think.
quests.turn_in_text:
They are the same hole. That is what I think and I have thought it for a year and there is no way to prove it from up here.

Something runs between them. Under us. East.

quests.title: Everything Points East
quests.description: Put it together: the brine, the wet scale, the light, the two with no floor.
quests.accept_text:
Sepp has brine. Hask has four shrike crops with water animals in them. Vizzi has a hundred and twenty feet of line that does not reach anything, twice, both on the east side. And there is light coming up out of the ground.

I am a surveyor. I do not get to say what that MEANS. I do get to say that every single one of those points the same direction, and I want one more set of readings before I write the sentence.
quests.turn_in_text:
East. All of it, east, toward the big hole with the water in it that the goblins are sitting on - a hole that was not there before the change either, like everything else I have had to measure.

Somebody over there needs to see my book and I am four years too busy to carry it.

quests.title: Four Carts
quests.description: Everything this camp owns has to fit on four carts and be gone in a day.
quests.accept_text:
Four carts. That is the rule and I did not make it, and we have struck camp in a day twice and both times I was glad about the rule and nobody else was.

The scavengers have been at the spare fittings. Brass, mostly, which they can sell and I cannot replace. Get it back.
quests.turn_in_text:
That is a cart's worth of brass. I know exactly what that is worth because I know exactly what everything here is worth, which is the entire job.

Prices have been mad since the day the ground changed, and brass has been the maddest of them.

quests.title: A Short Pantry
quests.description: There is food out here. It is a short list and she knows all of it now.
quests.accept_text:
A desert has a pantry. It is short and most of it is unpleasant and after four camps I know all of it.

Kodo is the bulk of it. Shrike, if you are quick and you do not mind the work. Go and get me enough for a fortnight and I will cook you something you will be rude about and finish.
quests.turn_in_text:
There. You were rude about it and you finished it.

Some of what I cook with came through with everybody else, you know. There are things growing in Tanaris now that have no business in a desert and they go in the pot like anything else.

Four camps. The food has got better every time and nobody expected that, including me.

quests.title: Peg Irons
quests.description: Survey stakes need iron and the crawlers keep eating it.
quests.accept_text:
I shod kodo for nine years and now I make peg irons, which is a sentence I try not to say out loud too often.

The crawlers go for them. Something in the iron, or something in the heat of it - Sepp has a theory and I have stopped listening. Bring me plate and I will line the next batch with it, and we will find out whether a crawler will chew through its own cousin.
quests.turn_in_text:
It will not. Six weeks and not a mark on them.

I have lined survey stakes with the shells of the things that eat survey stakes. I would like somebody to write that down somewhere it will be found.

quests.title: A Three-Month Contract
quests.description: He came out on a three-month contract two years and two camps ago.
quests.accept_text:
I came out with the second camp on a three-month contract.

That was two years and two camps ago and nobody has ever mentioned the contract again, including me.

I am not complaining and I would like that understood before I ask you for anything. Go south and make the run to the Throats survivable for a woman carrying glass, and I will tell you why I stayed.
quests.turn_in_text:
Because somebody has to be the one who is still here when the answer turns up.

That is it. That is the whole reason and it took me eight months to work it out and about four seconds to say.

quests.title: Four Years of Dates
quests.description: Her collapse log, east, to somebody who has been waiting four years for it.

objectives.label: Peska Vane's collapse log, to the surveyor at Lastwater

quests.accept_text:
Through the east gate, down into the hole with the water in it. There is a camp at the bottom and there is a tauren in it doing the same job I am doing from the other end.

I have every collapse date since this began and no theory at all. I am told she has four years of theory and has never once had a set of dates from inside a collapse field.

Neither of us knew the other existed. That is not a charming coincidence, it is a disgrace, and it is the ordinary condition of everybody who has worked on this since the sky changed.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Ulla Stormhollow reads the first twenty pages standing up, then sits down on a crate and reads the rest without saying anything.]

She has dates.

Four years I have had a shape with no numbers in it, and there is a goblin four days northwest who has been writing the numbers down the entire time and thought she was doing something else.

Tell her - no. I will write. Some things should not be carried by somebody else.

on_accept.name: Peska Vane's Collapse Log
on_accept.description: Eleven holes, four years, every date and bearing, in a very small hand.

quests.title: What She Said Back
quests.description: Carry the reply west, and the Sands finally get told what happened to them.

objectives.label: Ulla's reply, to Chief Surveyor Vane

quests.accept_text:
I have written it out. It is four pages and the first three are arithmetic she will be able to check herself, which is the only kind of letter worth sending to somebody like her.

The fourth page is what it means, and she is not going to like it, because it means her field is going to keep opening until somebody stops the thing that is doing it.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Peska reads it twice. Then she goes and stands by the peg for a while.]

It is not the ground.

Two years. Two years of me reading the hardpan and Hask listening to it and both of us trying to work out what was wrong with the ROCK, and the rock is fine. The rock has done nothing. The rock has been holding up exactly as well as rock does when there is water under it.

I am going to have to tell the camp. And then I am going to have to write to the port and tell them the answer to 'is a road possible' is 'ask whoever is at the bottom of that hole'.

on_accept.name: Ulla Stormhollow's Reply
on_accept.description: Four pages. Three of arithmetic and one of what it means.

quests.title: Down the Wide Sink
quests.description: Climb down the Wide Sink into the Dry Deep and walk to the Drained Sea.
quests.accept_text:
I have put a line down every hole on this map. Most of them it comes back up wet with nothing and you learn nothing.

The Wide Sink is different. The line goes slack. There is a FLOOR down there, and the debris has slumped into a ramp a person can walk.

Go down the Wide Sink. It is the big pit south-west of this camp. At the bottom you are in the Dry Deep. Keep going until the roof lifts and you cannot see the far wall. Peska calls that room the Drained Sea. Then come and tell me I am not imagining it.
quests.turn_in_text:
So it is one room. Not eleven holes. One enormous room with a roof that has fallen in eleven places.

I have been lowering lamps into the same cavern for two years from different sides and writing each one down as a separate hole.

unique_item_defs.name: Lamplit Sabatons
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Taken off something that had no business being at that depth.
unique_item_defs.label: Plate Boots (Sta/Def/Dodge)

unique_item_defs.name: Up-Through Belt
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Taken off something that had no business being at that depth.
unique_item_defs.label: Cloth Belt (Sta/Int/HP)

unique_item_defs.name: Rope-Hand's Knife
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Whatever wore this came from somewhere that still has a roof.
unique_item_defs.label: Dagger (Dodge/Parry)

quests.title: Up a Different Hole
quests.description: Walk the Dry Deep from shaft to shaft and find out which sinkholes join underground.
quests.accept_text:
Vizzi says it joins up down there. I want to know if she is right, because I lost a road down Nineteen Mile and I have always wondered where it went.

Go down into the Dry Deep by any hole that has a ramp. Find the daylight under Nineteen Mile Pit, the daylight under the Long Collapse and the daylight under the Underlight. If you can walk between all of them without coming up, then it is not a field of pits at all. It is a roof.
quests.turn_in_text:
All of them. You walked from one to the next under the desert.

Then my road did not fall into a hole. It fell into a country. That is somehow worse and I am glad to know it.

unique_item_defs.name: Cartfall Greaves
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Somebody was wearing this on an ordinary afternoon.
unique_item_defs.label: Plate Legs (Str/Sta/Crit)

unique_item_defs.name: Off-the-Box Sabatons
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Teamster's kit. The teamster is still here; most of them are not.
unique_item_defs.label: Mail Boots (Sta/Dodge/Parry)

unique_item_defs.name: Went-With-It Band
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Four years under sand and the buckles still work, which is the cruel part.
unique_item_defs.label: Ring (Int/Hit/SP)

quests.title: What Eats the Floor
quests.description: Kill Hollowing Oozes and Limestone Crawlers in the Dry Deep, where they eat the rock that holds the desert up.
quests.accept_text:
If there is one cavern under all of this then the question I am paid to answer has changed. It is no longer whether the pits are finished. It is whether the ROOF is.

The Hollowing Oozes eat limestone and the Limestone Crawlers nest in what the oozes leave. Up here they are a nuisance. Down in the Dry Deep they are working on the pillars.

Go down and thin them, the Hollowing Oozes and the Limestone Crawlers both, and look at what they have been eating while you are there.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then they are at the pillars. I thought they would be.

I can slow it. I cannot stop it. But a survey that says how long is a better survey than one that says nothing, and that is the first honest line I will have written in two years.

unique_item_defs.name: Struck-Camp Cuffs
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Marked in a very small hand with a date and a bearing.
unique_item_defs.label: Mail Bracers (Sta/Def/Dodge)

unique_item_defs.name: Peg-Iron Cuirass
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Marked in a very small hand with a date and a bearing.
unique_item_defs.label: Plate Chest (Str/Sta/Crit)

unique_item_defs.name: Chainman's Mace
unique_item_defs.flavor_text: Marked in a very small hand with a date and a bearing.
unique_item_defs.label: Mace (Sta/Armor/Parry)

quests.title: The Weight of the Floor
quests.description: Kill the Weight of the Floor, the thing that stands in the middle of the Drained Sea.
quests.accept_text:
There is something standing in the Drained Sea. My lamps find it and then they go out.

It is made of the same rock as the roof. I think it IS roof, a piece that came down whole and did not lie still. Peska's people will not go past it and I do not blame them.

Kill the Weight of the Floor. Go back down the Wide Sink, south-west of this camp, into the Dry Deep. It stands in the middle of the Drained Sea, the biggest room down there, and you will not mistake it for anything else.
quests.turn_in_text:
It is down. I felt it through the rope from up here.

The way further in is open, then. I do not know what is further in. Nobody has had a reason to find out until today.
